prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Dallas after a truck accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but first a quick question: do you need a lawyer right away (still in hospital / urgent deadlines), or do you want a short list of well-qualified Dallas firms to call this week? Also, do you prefer a local boutique firm or a large national firm?

While you answer, here’s something you can use immediately: how to pick which specific firms to call, what to ask them on the phone, and what to bring to the consultation.

Which firms to call (how to find good candidates quickly)
- Search for Dallas personal-injury lawyers who specifically advertise truck / commercial-vehicle experience. Trucking cases require specialized knowledge (FMCSA rules, complex insurance, accident reconstruction).
- Look for attorneys who: (1) have trial experience with truck cases, (2) use accident reconstruction experts, (3) have handled large settlements/verdicts against trucking companies, and (4) work on contingency (no fee unless they win).
- Sources to find names fast: Google Maps (“truck accident lawyer Dallas”), Texas Trial Lawyers Association, Dallas Bar Association lawyer referral, Avvo/Martindale-Hubbell profiles, and client reviews. Note any firm that lists “truck accidents,” “commercial vehicle,” or “catastrophic injury” as specialties.

Top questions to ask on your first phone call (keep it short — 5–10 minutes)
1. How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many have you tried to verdict?
2. Do you personally handle my case or pass it to associates? Who will be my main contact?
3. Have you worked cases against drivers’ trucking companies/insurers and obtained large settlements or verdicts?
4. Do you use accident reconstruction and medical experts? Will you advance those costs?
5. What is your fee structure and contingency percentage? Any other costs I should expect?
6. How long do you expect this type of case to take?
7. Can you provide recent results or references from truck-accident clients?

What to bring to the consultation (or have ready during a phone consult)
- Police accident report
- Photos/videos of the scene, vehicles, injuries
- Names and contact info for the truck driver, trucking company, witnesses
- Insurance information (your insurer and any info from other parties)
- Medical records, bills, ER records, notes about treatment and time off work
- Any correspondence from insurance companies

Immediate steps (if you haven’t already)
- Get medical treatment and follow doctors’ orders (document everything).
- Preserve evidence: photos, videos, damaged items, clothing.
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other side or sign anything without a lawyer.
- Preserve truck dashcam footage if possible (it’s often overwritten quickly).
- Report to your insurer and get a claim number, but avoid detailed recorded statements until you consult a lawyer.

If you want, I can:
- Draft a 30–60 second call script you can use when calling firms.
- Help you evaluate 3–5 specific Dallas firms if you want me to look them up now — tell me whether you prefer local boutiques or larger national firms, and whether your injuries are catastrophic (e.g., paralysis, amputation, TBI) or non-catastrophic.
